Founded in 2016 by Erica Jain, Cavan Klinsky, and Helen Corrigan, the company has raised $42M in total funding, including a $23M Series B in 2024 led by TCV. Healthie has approximately 135 employees and serves over 25,000 active clinical providers managing more than 10 million patient records and processing over 10 million appointments.\n     9→\n    10→Healthie positions itself as serving the \"underdogs of healthcare\" — independent practitioners, small group practices, and digital health startups that are typically underserved by legacy EHR vendors. The platform operates across two main go-to-market segments: (1) a direct SaaS product for individual clinicians and group practices, and (2) Healthie+, an API-first infrastructure offering for digital health companies that want to build custom clinical experiences on top of Healthie's backend. Key clinical specialties include behavioral health, nutrition/dietetics, women's health, chronic care management, musculoskeletal care, health coaching, substance use treatment, and longevity medicine. Notable customers include Found (weight management), Klarity Health (psychiatric services), GEM Health (sleep disorders), Isaac Health (dementia care), and Teal Health (women's health).\n    11→\n    12→## Product: Healthie\n    13→\n    14→CHPL IDs: 11055\n    15→\n    16→### What It Is\n    17→\n    18→Healthie is an all-in-one EHR, practice management, and patient engagement platform. The certified product (\"Healthie Cures 1,\" certified 2022-12-07) appears to be the entire platform — there is no indication that the certified module is a subset of a larger product. Healthie is a single, unified cloud-hosted platform with web and mobile (iOS/Android) apps for both providers and patients. The platform is built on Ruby/Postgres with React/React Native frontends, and exposes its full functionality through a GraphQL API.\n    19→\n    20→The certification profile is broad, covering clinical data (a)(3)-(5), (a)(12), (a)(14); transitions of care (b)(1)-(3); patient portal (e)(1); clinical quality measures (c)(1)-(3); FHIR APIs (g)(7)-(10); and health information exchange (h)(1). This suggests a comprehensive clinical system, not a narrow module.\n    21→\n    22→### Users & Market\n    23→\n    24→**Day-to-day users include:**\n    25→- Clinicians: nutritionists, dietitians, therapists, psychiatrists, health coaches, nurse practitioners, physicians across multiple specialties\n    26→- Practice administrators and billing staff\n    27→- Patients/clients (via the patient portal and mobile app)\n    28→\n    29→**Settings served:**\n    30→- Solo practitioners and small group practices\n    31→- Digital health startups building virtual-first care platforms\n    32→- Multi-location wellness groups (e.g., 15+ clinicians)\n    33→- Non-profit social services organizations\n    34→- Enterprise organizations requiring scalable API infrastructure\n    35→\n    36→**Scale:** 25,000+ active providers, 10M+ patient records, 10M+ appointments. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01T4gNWXT39kX5NejTvFTc1s","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01LM4s2fcmEGbdMHbwuCfTGX","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"# Try extracting between article markers\npython3 -c \"\nimport re\nwith open('/tmp/healthie-ehi-page.html') as f:\n    html = f.read()\n# Find the article content\nmatch = re.search(r'id=\\\"fullArticle\\\"[^>]*>(.*?)</article>', html, re.DOTALL)\nif match:\n    text = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', match.group(1))\n    text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text).strip()\n    print(text[:8000])\nelse:\n    print('No article found')\n\"","description":"Extract article text using Python"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":333,"cache_read_input_tokens":37831,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":333},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"354678a7-b05b-4118-96a4-c336d8bd88a2","uuid":"86b92100-c915-4be0-91e2-32d56aab50f0"}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LM4s2fcmEGbdMHbwuCfTGX","type":"tool_result","content":"(b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export This document describes Healthie’s support for ONC §170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information export. Per (b)(10) ONC Certification, Healthie supports two types of electronic health information exports: Single patient System/patient population IN THIS ARTICLE: What is Electronic Health Information (EHI)? Generating an Export Export Format What is Electronic Health Information (EHI)? Electronic Health Information (EHI) refers to “electronic protected health information” (ePHI) to the extent that it would be included in a designated record set as defined: Designated record set &nbsp;means: A group of records maintained by or for a covered entity that is: The medical records and billing records about individuals maintained by or for a covered health care provider The enrollment, payment, claims adjudication, and case or medical management record systems maintained by or for a health plan; or Records used, in whole or in part, by or for the covered entity to make decisions about individuals. For purposes of this paragraph, the term record means any item, collection, or grouping of information that includes protected health. EHI does not include psychotherapy notes as defined in 45 CFR 164.501 or information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil, criminal, or administrative action or proceeding. The EHI definition represents the same ePHI that an individual would have the right to access under the HIPAA Privacy Rule. Generating an Export A user can initiate a single-patient export by navigating to a patient’s profile and viewing the Charting section. The report can be generated by an organization member with the “Can generate organization report” setting enabled or by a non-organization user. System exports can only be initiated by an administrator. The patient population data export is handled by the Healthie Support team as it depends on size of data, time and efforts required to manage the server resources. Please email&nbsp; hello@gethealthie.com &nbsp;with the subject line “ Patient Population b10 export request ” to initiate the process. Export Format Overview: The EHI Export process generates CSV files, PDF files, and a folder per patient that are presented as a compressed zip file. For the patient population export, the zip file contains one directory for each patient. The directories are named &lt;FirstName&gt; &lt;LastName&gt; &lt;uniqueidentifier&gt; . The contents of each directory are the same as the individual patient export. Further detail on each file is below. Within the zip file the following csv files, PDFs, folder, and HTML page are generated per patient: Addresses.csv Allergies.csv CarePlans.csv Charting.pdf client_metrics.csv Client_Overview.csv Client_User_Groups.csv cms1500s.csv Diagnoses.csv Documents folder Family_and_Contacts.csv Food_Intolerances.csv Food_Preferences.csv Food_Sensitivities.csv FoodEntry.csv format.html Goals.csv Insurance_authorizations.csv Insurance.csv journal_entries.pdf Medications.csv Messages.csv MetricEntry.csv MirrorEntry.csv NoteEntry.csv Other_Care_Team_Members.csv Packages.csv Payments.csv Policies.csv PoopEntry.csv Provider.csv Recommendations.csv Referring_Physicians.csv SleepEntry.csv superbills.csv SymptomEntry.csv WaterIntakeEntry.csv WorkoutEntry.csv Notes: Whereas any rows or cells are blank, there is no data for the patient. All data in the CSV files will be exported as a string. File format: Addresses.csv format and data elements: Columns Address Line1 Address Line2 City State Zip Country Allergies.csv format and data elements: Columns Allergen Code System Name Category Category Type Onset Date Reaction Reaction Code Reaction Code System Name Reaction Type Code Reaction Type Code System Name Reaction Type Name CarePlans.csv format and data elements: Columns Data Notes Description Is Hidden true or false Name Charting.pdf format and data elements: The pdf contains all charting notes for the patient. Format and data elements are specific to an organization’s and patient’s charting notes. client_metrics.csv format and data elements: Columns Data notes Unique ID Client Current Status Active or Inactive Client Group Tags Client’s Provider Metric Category Metric categories (presented as rows in the csv file): Weight, Body Fat %, Waist Circumference, Height (in) Dates Year-Mo-Day CSV includes a column header for each day the patient has been active. The rows are populated with Metric Category patient For example: Client_Overview.csv format and data elements: Columns Data notes First Name Legal Name Last Name Email Mobile Phone number Additional phone number Gender Pronouns DOB Year-Mo-Day Current weight Height Client Since Year-Mo-Day 00:00:00 UTC Quick Notes Client_User_Groups.csv format and data elements: Columns Name Users Count cms1500s.csv format and data elements: For each CMS for the patient, there is a row in the CSV Columns Data notes Date of Service Year-Mo-Day Create Date Year/Mo/Day 00:00:00 CDT Provider Unique ID Client Current Status Active or Inactive Client Date of Birth Year/Mo/Day Client Group Referring Physician Units Total Billed Status Amount Reimbursed Date Reimbursed Copay Outstanding Balance Primary Policy Name Primary Policy Member ID Number Primary Policy Group Number Primary Insurance Type Secondary Policy Name Secondary Policy Member ID Number Secondary Policy Group Number Secondary Insurance Type Service Facility Procedure Codes Diagnoses.csv format and data elements: Columns Data notes Code Active true or false Onset Date Year-Mo-Day End Date Year-Mo-Day Documents folder format and data elements: The Documents folder will contain all documents saved in the patient’s Documents page in Healthie. The documents will be exported in the original format as saved in Healthie. The documents file structure will also correspond to the folder structure as created in the patient’s Documents page in Healthie. Family_and_Contacts.csv format and data elements: Columns First Name Last Name Email Phone Number Relationship Food_Intolerances.csv format and data elements: Columns Allergen Code Allergen Code System Name Category Category Type Onset Date Reaction Reaction Code Reaction Code System Name Reaction Type Code Reaction Type Code System Name Reaction Type Name Food_Preferences.csv format and data elements: Columns Allergen Code Allergen Code System Name Category Category Type Onset Date Reaction Reaction Code Reaction Code System Name Reaction Type Code Reaction Type Code System Name Reaction Type Name Food_Sensitivities.csv format and data elements: Columns Allergen Code Allergen Code System Name Category Category Type Onset Date Reaction Reaction Code Reaction Code System Name Reaction Type Code Reaction Type Code System Name Reaction Type Name FoodEntry.csv format and data elements: Columns Data notes Category Code Code System Name Description Ed Posthunger Ed Prehunger Emotions Entries in Average Hide from Main Feed true or false Is Meal Template true or false Metric Stat Other Symptom Perceived Hungriness Previous Water Intake Stat Reflection Subentries Count Symptoms Third Party Source Unit Value Viewed true or false format.html Within this html page you can find&nbsp; this publicly accessible hyperlink &nbsp;that describes the export format Goals.csv format and data elements: For each Goal for the patient, there is a row in the CSV Columns Description Due Date Metric Target Name Repeat Start On Subgoals Count Insurance_authorizations.csv format and data elements: Columns Unique ID Client preferred name Client legal name Client middle name Client last name Current status Client group Client's provider Client date of birth Client gender Client phone number Date of first appointment Date of last appointment Billing Type Policy Insurance 1 Member ID Insurance 1 Group ID Referring Physician Authorization Number Number of Visits Authorized Number of Visits Used Effective Start Date Effective End Date Insura","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"354678a7-b05b-4118-96a4-c336d8bd88a2","uuid":"a9a16de1-fdbf-4adb-b9a2-9b5a1205ef0a","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"(b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export This document describes Healthie’s support for ONC §170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information export. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0136krg1dzi2CiiuyBiC7JsA","type":"tool_result","content":"Healthie: ONC Certification The ONC Health IT Certification Program (Certification Program) ensures that Certified Health Information Technology meets the technological capability, functionality, and security requirements adopted by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).&nbsp;EHR providers, like Healthie, can volunteer to have the ONC review their platform for certification. Healthie’s Early EHR certification is 2015 compliant and has been certified by an ONC-ACB in accordance with the applicable certification criteria adopted by the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. Via Healthie, providers will be able to utilize key functionalities including direct messaging, reimbursements for meaningful use (eCQMs and MIPS) and FHIR as a result of Healthie meeting ONC certification requirements. IN THIS ARTICLE: A Note on Healthie's Security and Privacy Measures Direct Messaging on Healthie FHIR API on Healthie (b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export on Healthie Clinical Quality Measure (eCQMs) on Healthie Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture (CCDA) Import and Export on Healthie A Note on&nbsp;Healthie's Security and Privacy Measures Healthie's platform meets the highest certification standards for data security and privacy, leveraging industry standards to secure data for you and your clients. Our customers can rest easy knowing the the Healthie platform meets rigorous Health IT requirements. If you're a current Healthie customer reach out to your Customer Success Manager to learn more and for updates. If you're not a Healthie customer yet, but want to learn more, please email hello@gethealthie.com with your questions. Direct Messaging on Healthie Direct Messaging on Healthie, as part of our ONC certification, enables providers to securely send and receive health information.&nbsp;Direct Messaging is a HIPAA-compliant, easy to use feature that ensures that orders, electronic health records, and other protected health information are securely transmitted by the person who they say they are. Direct Messaging within Healthie not only gives providers access to a nationwide directory of covered entities, but also simplifies the process of sending and receiving referrals as digital structured content making transmitted documents much more useful than faxing.&nbsp; Learn more here . FHIR API on Healthie Healthie’s ONC certified FHIR API works as an add-on layer on top of the main Healthie application. Utilizing this functionality, supported by&nbsp; Aidbox , organizations and providers can access, search and modify electronic health records and seamlessly exchange data between healthcare IT systems. Learn more here . (b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export on Healthie As part of its b10 ONC Certification, Healthie can provide our customers with the capability to efficiently export single and multi-patient Electronic Health Information in a secure and timely manner. Healthie can also implement any type of export capability, as long as it supports the two use cases of single patient and patient population EHI export functionalities. EHI export must also be self-service and able to be executed at any time the user chooses and without subsequent developer assistance to operate. Finally, certified Health IT Module must be able to limit users who can perform an EHI export. Learn more about (b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export here . Clinical Quality Measures (eCQMs) on Healthie As part of its ONC Certification, Healthie can capture, export, calculate and report on measured meaningful use data through Clinical Quality Measures (eCQMs).&nbsp; eCQMs are used by the Centers for Medicare &amp; Medicaid Services (CMS) in a variety of quality reporting and value-based purchasing programs. Learn more here . Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture (CCDA) Import and Export on Healthie As part of its ONC Certification, Healthie can share clinical data via the Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture (CCDA) format, which makes Healthie interoperable in a standard way with other sources of healthcare data (e.g., EHRs). The&nbsp;HL7 Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture&nbsp;(CCDA) is an XML-based markup standard which provides a library of&nbsp;Clinical Document Architecture (CDA)&nbsp;formatted documents. Clinical documents using the CCDA standards are exchanged billions of times annually in the United States. All certified EHRs&nbsp;in the United States are required to export medical data using the CCDA standard. Learn more here .","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"354678a7-b05b-4118-96a4-c336d8bd88a2","uuid":"4f81b1a1-26d7-42b0-9f7f-e77fd97506bc","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"Healthie: ONC Certification The ONC Health IT Certification Program (Certification Program) ensures that Certified Health Information Technology meets the technological capability, functionality, and security requirements adopted by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).&nbsp;EHR providers, like Healthie, can volunteer to have the ONC review their platform for certification. Healthie’s Early EHR certification is 2015 compliant and has been certified by an ONC-ACB in accordance with the applicable certification criteria adopted by the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. Via Healthie, providers will be able to utilize key functionalities including direct messaging, reimbursements for meaningful use (eCQMs and MIPS) and FHIR as a result of Healthie meeting ONC certification requirements. Our customers can rest easy knowing the the Healthie platform meets rigorous Health IT requirements. If you're a current Healthie customer reach out to your Customer Success Manager to learn more and for updates. If you're not a Healthie customer yet, but want to learn more, please email hello@gethealthie.com with your questions. Direct Messaging on Healthie Direct Messaging on Healthie, as part of our ONC certification, enables providers to securely send and receive health information.&nbsp;Direct Messaging is a HIPAA-compliant, easy to use feature that ensures that orders, electronic health records, and other protected health information are securely transmitted by the person who they say they are. Utilizing this functionality, supported by&nbsp; Aidbox , organizations and providers can access, search and modify electronic health records and seamlessly exchange data between healthcare IT systems. Learn more here . Healthie can also implement any type of export capability, as long as it supports the two use cases of single patient and patient population EHI export functionalities. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EbxReUvf87p52KtQNgkSJT","type":"tool_result","content":"Export or Transfer Healthie Account Data Healthie makes it simple for you to obtain data from your Healthie account. While we do not support transferring data from one Healthie account to another, you can always request an export of your data, and then request an import into your new account (more information here ).&nbsp; With Healthie, you can leverage our built in reports functionality to have visibility into data on your patients, appointments, billing and more. You can also download chart notes and documents for your clients, as well as any templates in your account. Note : If you would like Healthie to export your client data and documents for you, we offer this assistance to paid Healthie memberships (see information below). Exporting or Transferring Client Data&nbsp; There may be several reasons that you are looking to export or transfer business and client information from the platform. This may include: You are seeking to run business analyses for your internal use You are submitting information for an insurance billing audit You are looking for a backup of your business and client records You will be canceling your Healthie subscription You are creating another Healthie provider account , and would like to transfer client data Note: While Healthie can help with importing data from one account to another (that the account owner provides), we aren't able to conduct a true data transfer behind the scenes.&nbsp; Ways to Export Data from Healthie Healthie makes it easy to pull business and client information from the system. Here is information that can be downloaded from the system: 1. Leverage Healthie Reports Pull key business and client information by generating valuable reports in your Reporting tab . Particularly, you may want to export the Client List report, which is your list of clients and relevant client information. This report can be imported into another Healthie account if your are transitioning accounts.&nbsp; 2. Download Client Chart Notes or Documents You can download existing documents or charting notes from your current account for individual clients. 3. Download Intake Form and Charting Templates You can download PDFs of Forms that you have created following these instructions .&nbsp; Have a form you'd like to migrate to another Healthie provider account? Share your form with your new provider account email address. Once shared, the forms will be visible to you in your forms library. Editing these forms in your new account will not affect the original form from your first account.&nbsp; 4. Request a File Data Export If you would like assistance with downloading all of your clients charting notes and documents, you can request an export here: File Data Export Request . Please note that our standard export only includes client charting notes and documents as a Zip file, which will be placed in your Healthie profile under “Documents” for you to access. This process does take time so if you need data immediately, we recommend using reports or downloading client files per the instructions above.&nbsp; Note: Only Healthie account owners can request and receive an export.&nbsp; Download a Summary of Your Client's Logged Entries If you'd like to download (and share) a complete record of your client's logged journal entries, you have the option to do so within charting.&nbsp; Navigate to&nbsp; Client &gt; Charting &gt; Download Client Summary A PDF will populate in a new browser tab for you to download and save to your local device as needed.&nbsp; Notes &amp; FAQs Follow the steps outlined here to&nbsp; import client data &nbsp;into your Healthie provider account (ie. if you are creating a second Healthie provider account).&nbsp; For any export we create of client lists, that request will need to come from the assigned provider (or account admin) to ensure complete transparency every step of the way. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011D7k76zBw72CbP3Zre8FVS","type":"tool_result","content":"Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture (CCDA) Import and Export on Healthie This document describes Healthie’s support for sharing clinical data via the Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture (CCDA) format part of its ONC Certification, which makes Healthie interoperable in a standard way with other sources of healthcare data (e.g., EHRs). The&nbsp;HL7 Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture&nbsp;(CCDA) is an XML-based markup standard which provides a library of&nbsp;Clinical Document Architecture (CDA)&nbsp;formatted documents. Clinical documents using the CCDA standards are exchanged billions of times annually in the United States. All certified EHRs&nbsp;in the United States are required to export medical data using the CCDA standard. Note : CCDA Import and Export is only available to Healthie Enterprise level customers at this time.&nbsp;Customers can reach out to hello@gethealthie.com to enable this functionality for their accounts. IN THIS ARTICLE: Add a Client via CCDA File Importing and/or Exporting a CCDA File Add a Client via CCDA File In order to add a client via a CCDA File, navigate to your Clients tab (left navigation sidebar). Click on Action ( ... ) &gt; Add Client via CCDA file . When you click on \" Import CCDA File \", select the appropriate XML file on your local device, and click on \" Add via Uploaded File .\" You will see a green confirmation banner with a \" View Client \" button when your client (e.g. Jeremy Bates) has been successfully added from your CCDA XML file. If you wish to view the newly created client's profile, click on \" View Client .\" In the case that there is an issue with the XML file you've uploaded that prevents the client from being created, you will see a red error banner similar to the one shown below. We recommend following the best practices outlined in this \" View Guidance on CCDA Files \" document to troubleshoot if necessary. If you are interested in importing multiple clients, learn more here . Importing and/or Exporting a CCDA File Healthie provides you with the ability to export a CCDA file. In order to do this, navigate to Clients (left navigation sidebar) &gt; select Client Name . After you reach the Client Overview page, click on the Charting tab. You will now see a box labeled \" Records \" which allows you to: Download Client Journaling Summary View the current client's CCDA data by clicking \" View CCDA Information \" Import CCDA File Export CCDA File Importing a CCDA File When you click on \" Import CCDA File \", select the appropriate XML file on your local device, and click on \" Add via Uploaded File .\" When this XML file is successfully uploaded, you will be navigated to a new page called \" CCDA Reconciliation .\" Exporting a CCDA File When you click on \" Export CCDA File \", a CCDA file will be created and added to this clients' private Documents (when you navigate to Client Name &gt; Charting &gt; Documents &gt; View Documents ). {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01UMccYL79eDhdRFFcxoQCEe","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01T4K6XJqsDr2y3Gz4KPvnsH","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"python3 << 'PYEOF'\nimport re\nwith open('/tmp/healthie-ehi-page.html') as f:\n    html = f.read()\nmatch = re.search(r'id=\"fullArticle\"[^>]*>(.*?)</article>', html, re.DOTALL)\nif match:\n    article = match.group(1)\n    fmt_start = article.find('Export Format')\n    if fmt_start > 0:\n        section = article[fmt_start:fmt_start+4000]\n        print(section)\nPYEOF","description":"View raw HTML of export format section"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":276,"cache_read_input_tokens":56167,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":276},"output_tokens":25,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"354678a7-b05b-4118-96a4-c336d8bd88a2","uuid":"f2d7b884-fd21-4b1b-a498-f2424a14fdc0"}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01T4K6XJqsDr2y3Gz4KPvnsH","type":"tool_result","content":"Export Format</a></li>\n </ul>\n</div>\n<hr role=\"separator\">\n<h2 id=\"What-is-Electronic-Health-Information-EHI-KViuE\">What is Electronic Health Information (EHI)?</h2>\n<p>Electronic Health Information (EHI) refers to “electronic protected health information” (ePHI) to the extent that it would be included in a designated record set as defined:</p>\n<ul>\n <li><em>Designated record set</em>&nbsp;means:\n  <ul>\n   <li>A group of records maintained by or for a covered entity that is:\n    <ul>\n     <li>The medical records and billing records about individuals maintained by or for a covered health care provider</li>\n     <li>The enrollment, payment, claims adjudication, and case or medical management record systems maintained by or for a health plan; or</li>\n     <li>Records used, in whole or in part, by or for the covered entity to make decisions about individuals.</li>\n    </ul></li>\n  </ul></li>\n</ul>\n<p>For purposes of this paragraph, the term record means any item, collection, or grouping of information that includes protected health. EHI does not include psychotherapy notes as defined in 45 CFR 164.501 or information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil, criminal, or administrative action or proceeding.</p>\n<p>The EHI definition represents the same ePHI that an individual would have the right to access under the HIPAA Privacy Rule.</p>\n<hr role=\"separator\">\n<h2 id=\"Generating-an-Export-WBpPg\">Generating an Export</h2>\n<br>\n<p>A user can initiate a single-patient export by navigating to a patient’s profile and viewing the Charting section. The report can be generated by an organization member with the “Can generate organization report” setting enabled or by a non-organization user.</p>\n<br>\n<p>System exports can only be initiated by an administrator. The patient population data export is handled by the Healthie Support team as it depends on size of data, time and efforts required to manage the server resources. Please email&nbsp;<a href=\"mailto:hello@gethealthie.com\">hello@gethealthie.com</a>&nbsp;with the subject line “<b>Patient Population b10 export request</b>” to initiate the process.</p>\n<hr role=\"separator\">\n<h2 id=\"Export-Format-zRlWB\">Export Format</h2>\n<br>\n<p><u><strong>Overview:</strong></u></p>\n<p>The EHI Export process generates CSV files, PDF files, and a folder per patient that are presented as a compressed zip file.</p>\n<p>For the patient population export, the zip file contains one directory for each patient. Format</a></li>\n </ul>\n</div>\n<hr role=\"separator\">\n<h2 id=\"What-is-Electronic-Health-Information-EHI-KViuE\">What is Electronic Health Information (EHI)?</h2>\n<p>Electronic Health Information (EHI) refers to “electronic protected health information” (ePHI) to the extent that it would be included in a designated record set as defined:</p>\n<ul>\n <li><em>Designated record set</em>&nbsp;means:\n  <ul>\n   <li>A group of records maintained by or for a covered entity that is:\n    <ul>\n     <li>The medical records and billing records about individuals maintained by or for a covered health care provider</li>\n     <li>The enrollment, payment, claims adjudication, and case or medical management record systems maintained by or for a health plan; or</li>\n     <li>Records used, in whole or in part, by or for the covered entity to make decisions about individuals.</li>\n    </ul></li>\n  </ul></li>\n</ul>\n<p>For purposes of this paragraph, the term record means any item, collection, or grouping of information that includes protected health. EHI does not include psychotherapy notes as defined in 45 CFR 164.501 or information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil, criminal, or administrative action or proceeding.</p>\n<p>The EHI definition represents the same ePHI that an individual would have the right to access under the HIPAA Privacy Rule.</p>\n<hr role=\"separator\">\n<h2 id=\"Generating-an-Export-WBpPg\">Generating an Export</h2>\n<br>\n<p>A user can initiate a single-patient export by navigating to a patient’s profile and viewing the Charting section. The report can be generated by an organization member with the “Can generate organization report” setting enabled or by a non-organization user.</p>\n<br>\n<p>System exports can only be initiated by an administrator. bun\n/**\n * Extracts the Healthie EHI Export data dictionary from the downloaded HTML page\n * into a structured JSON format.\n *\n * Usage: bun run extract-data-dictionary.ts\n *\n * Input: ../ehi-export-page.html\n * Output: ./data-dictionary.json, ./extraction-log.json\n */\n\nimport { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from \"fs\";\nimport { join, dirname } from \"path\";\n\nconst scriptDir = dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);\nconst inputPath = join(scriptDir, \"..\", \"ehi-export-page.html\");\nconst outputPath = join(scriptDir, \"data-dictionary.json\");\nconst logPath = join(scriptDir, \"extraction-log.json\");\n\ninterface Column {\n  name: string;\n  data_notes: string | null;\n}\n\ninterface ExportFile {\n  filename: string;\n  type: \"csv\" | \"pdf\" | \"html\" | \"folder\";\n  description: string | null;\n  columns: Column[];\n  row_semantics: string | null; // e.g. \"For each CMS for the patient, there is a row in the CSV\"\n}\n\ninterface DataDictionary {\n  source_url: string;\n  extraction_date: string;\n  export_overview: {\n    format: string;\n    population_export_structure: string;\n    notes: string[];\n  };\n  export_generation: {\n    single_patient: string;\n    population: string;\n  };\n  files: ExportFile[];\n  total_files: number;\n  total_csv_files: number;\n  total_columns: number;\n}\n\nconst html = readFileSync(inputPath, \"utf-8\");\n\n// Extract article content\nconst articleMatch = html.match(/id=\"fullArticle\"[^>]*>(.*?)<\\/article>/s);\nif (!articleMatch) {\n  console.error(\"Could not find article content\");\n  process.exit(1);\n}\nconst article = articleMatch[1];\n\n// Extract the file list from the bullet list\nconst fileListMatch = article.match(\n  /Within the zip file the following.*?<ul>(.*?)<\\/ul>/s\n);\nconst fileListItems: string[] = [];\nif (fileListMatch) {\n  const items = fileListMatch[1].matchAll(/<li>(.*?)<\\/li>/gs);\n  for (const m of items) {\n    const clean = m[1].replace(/<[^>]+>/g, \"\").trim();\n    if (clean) fileListItems.push(clean);\n  }\n}\n\n// Extract notes after the file list\nconst notesMatch = article.match(\n  /Notes:<\\/p>\\s*<ul>(.*?)<\\/ul>/s\n);\nconst exportNotes: string[] = [];\nif (notesMatch) {\n  const items = notesMatch[1].matchAll(/<li>(.*?)<\\/li>/gs);\n  for (const m of items) {\n    const clean = m[1].replace(/<[^>]+>/g, \"\").replace(/&nbsp;/g, \" \").replace(/\\s+/g, \" \").trim();\n    if (clean) exportNotes.push(clean);\n  }\n}\n\n// Parse each file's format definition\n// Pattern: <u>Filename format and data elements:</u> or <u>Filename format and data elements</u>\n// followed by optional description paragraph, then a <table>\n\nconst files: ExportFile[] = [];\nconst parseErrors: Array<{ filename: string; error: string }> = [];\n\n// Split by file format sections\nconst fileSections = article.split(/<p><u>/g).slice(1); // skip everything before first file def\n\nfor (const section of fileSections) {\n  // Extract filename from the underlined header\n  const headerMatch = section.match(\n    /^([\\w_.]+(?:\\.csv|\\.pdf|\\.html)?)\\s+format and data elements:?<\\/u><\\/p>/i\n  );\n  if (!headerMatch) {\n    // Could be a non-file underlined section\n    continue;\n  }\n  const rawFilename = headerMatch[1];\n\n  // Determine file type\n  let type: \"csv\" | \"pdf\" | \"html\" | \"folder\" = \"csv\";\n  let filename = rawFilename;\n  if (rawFilename.endsWith(\".pdf\")) type = \"pdf\";\n  else if (rawFilename.endsWith(\".html\")) type = \"html\";\n  else if (!rawFilename.includes(\".\")) {\n    // Check if it's in fileListItems with an extension\n    const match = fileListItems.find(\n      (f) => f.toLowerCase().startsWith(rawFilename.toLowerCase())\n    );\n    if (match) filename = match;\n    if (filename.endsWith(\".pdf\")) type = \"pdf\";\n    else if (filename === \"Documents folder\") type = \"folder\";\n  }\n\n  // Extract description (paragraph text before table)\n  let description: string | null = null;\n  let rowSemantics: string | null = null;\n\n  // Look for paragraphs between the header and the table\n  const beforeTable = section.split(/<table>/)[0];\n  const paragraphs = beforeTable.matchAll(/<p>([^<].*?)<\\/p>/gs);\n  const descParts: string[] = [];\n  for (const p of paragraphs) {\n    const text = p[1]\n      .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, \"\")\n      .replace(/&nbsp;/g, \" \")\n      .replace(/&lt;/g, \"<\")\n      .replace(/&gt;/g, \">\")\n      .replace(/&amp;/g, \"&\")\n      .replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n      .trim();\n    if (text && !text.startsWith(\"For example\")) {\n      if (text.match(/^For each .* there is a row/i)) {\n        rowSemantics = text;\n      } else {\n        descParts.push(text);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  if (descParts.length > 0) description = descParts.join(\" \");\n\n  // Extract table columns\n  const columns: Column[] = [];\n  const tableMatch = section.match(/<table>(.*?)<\\/table>/s);\n  if (tableMatch) {\n    const tableHtml = tableMatch[1];\n    const rows = tableHtml.matchAll(/<tr>(.*?)<\\/tr>/gs);\n    let hasDataNotes = false;\n    let isHeaderRow = true;\n\n    for (const row of rows) {\n      const rowHtml = row[1];\n      // Check if header row\n      if (isHeaderRow) {\n        hasDataNotes = /Data [Nn]otes/i.test(rowHtml);\n        isHeaderRow = false;\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      // Extract cells\n      const cells = [...rowHtml.matchAll(/<t[dh]>(.*?)<\\/t[dh]>/gs)];\n      if (cells.length > 0) {\n        const colName = cells[0][1]\n          .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, \"\")\n          .replace(/&nbsp;/g, \" \")\n          .replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n          .trim();\n\n        let dataNotes: string | null = null;\n        if (hasDataNotes && cells.length > 1) {\n          const raw = cells[1][1]\n            .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, \"\")\n            .replace(/&nbsp;/g, \" \")\n            .replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n            .trim();\n          if (raw) dataNotes = raw;\n        }\n\n        if (colName) {\n          columns.push({ name: colName, data_notes: dataNotes });\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  files.push({\n    filename,\n    type,\n    description,\n    columns,\n    row_semantics: rowSemantics,\n  });\n}\n\n// Cross-check against the file list\nconst parsedFilenames = new Set(files.map((f) => f.filename.toLowerCase()));\nconst listedFiles = fileListItems.map((f) => f.toLowerCase());\nconst missingParsed = listedFiles.filter((f) => {\n  // Check if any parsed file matches\n  return !files.some(\n    (pf) =>\n      pf.filename.toLowerCase() === f ||\n      pf.filename.toLowerCase() + \".csv\" === f ||\n      pf.filename.toLowerCase() === f.replace(\" folder\", \"\")\n  );\n});\n\nconst dataDictionary: DataDictionary = {\n  source_url:\n    \"https://help.gethealthie.com/article/1200-b10-electronic-health-information-export-on-healthie\",\n  extraction_date: new Date().toISOString().split(\"T\")[0],\n  export_overview: {\n    format:\n      \"CSV files, PDF files, and a Documents folder per patient, presented as a compressed zip file\",\n    population_export_structure:\n      \"One directory per patient named <FirstName><LastName><uniqueidentifier>\",\n    notes: exportNotes,\n  },\n  export_generation: {\n    single_patient:\n      \"Navigate to patient profile > Charting section. Requires 'Can generate organization report' permission or non-organization user.\",\n    population:\n      \"Administrator-only. Handled by Healthie Support team. Email hello@gethealthie.com with subject 'Patient Population b10 export request'.\",\n  },\n  files,\n  total_files: files.length,\n  total_csv_files: files.filter((f) => f.type === \"csv\").length,\n  total_columns: files.reduce((sum, f) => sum + f.columns.length, 0),\n};\n\nwriteFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify(dataDictionary, null, 2));\n\nconst log = {\n  extraction_date: new Date().toISOString(),\n  input_file: inputPath,\n  output_file: outputPath,\n  total_files_in_listing: fileListItems.length,\n  total_files_parsed: files.length,\n  total_columns_extracted: dataDictionary.total_columns,\n  files_in_listing: fileListItems,\n  files_parsed: files.map((f) => f.filename),\n  missing_from_parse: missingParsed,\n  parse_errors: parseErrors,\n  files_by_type: {\n    csv: files.filter((f) => f.type === \"csv\").length,\n    pdf: files.filter((f) => f.type === \"pdf\").length,\n    html: files.filter((f) => f.type === \"html\").length,\n    folder: files.filter((f) => f.type === \"folder\").length,\n  },\n};\n\nwriteFileSync(logPath, JSON.stringify(log, null, 2));\n\nconsole.log(`Extracted ${files.length} file definitions with ${dataDictionary.total_columns} total columns`);\nconsole.log(`Listed files: ${fileListItems.length}, Parsed: ${files.length}`);\nif (missingParsed.length > 0) {\n  console.log(`Missing from parse: ${missingParsed.join(\", \")}`);\n}\nconsole.log(`Output: ${outputPath}`);\nconsole.log(`Log: ${logPath}`);\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":671,"cache_read_input_tokens":61163,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":671},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"354678a7-b05b-4118-96a4-c336d8bd88a2","uuid":"ff762209-4752-45cc-b2d3-f2102e0dbda4"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_012zJ44uwszS2ETnWMKS8rxB","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01J3eXzBeM11koDEPnXi68gQ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/healthie--healthie/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Healthie — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-16\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://help.gethealthie.com/article/1200-b10-electronic-health-information-export-on-healthie\n- CHPL IDs: 11055\n- Product: Healthie, version \"Cures 1\", certified 2022-12-07\n- Developer: Healthie (contact: compliance@gethealthie.com)\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe**: `curl -sI -L \"https://help.gethealthie.com/article/1200-b10-electronic-health-information-export-on-healthie\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'` returned HTTP 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`, 53,330 bytes. No redirects. The URL is served by a HelpScout Docs knowledge base hosted on Caddy/Istio.\n\n2. **Page download**: `curl -sL \"https://help.gethealthie.com/article/1200-b10-electronic-health-information-export-on-healthie\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o ehi-export-page.html`. The page loaded fully without JavaScript; the article body is in the HTML source, not loaded via SPA.\n\n3. **Link inventory**: Extracted all links from the `#fullArticle` element. The page contains only:\n   - Internal anchor links (#What-is-Electronic-Health-Information-EHI-KViuE, #Generating-an-Export-WBpPg, #Export-Format-zRlWB)\n   - A mailto link (hello@gethealthie.com)\n   - A broken link (`href=\"#undefined\"`) labeled \"this publicly accessible hyperlink\" that should point to format.html (included within each export ZIP)\n   - No downloadable files (PDF, ZIP, JSON, etc.) linked from the page\n\n4. **File search**: `grep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|csv|json)...\"'` found no downloadable artifacts.\n\n5. **Image download**: One embedded image — a screenshot example of client_metrics.csv format: `curl -sL \"https://d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5bbe96a22c7d3a04dd5b8761/images/6567bb962edfc966c355e31c/file-owoQwAwIzc.png\"`.\n\n6. **Browser verification**: Navigated in Chrome, took screenshots of the page top, \"Generating an Export\" section, \"Export Format\" section, and full page. All content rendered correctly; no hidden content behind accordions or JavaScript interactions.\n\n7. **Related articles search**: Searched Healthie help site for \"EHI export\" and browsed the \"EHR & Billing\" category. Found:\n   - [ONC Certification overview](https://help.gethealthie.com/article/1091-onc-certification) — hub page that links to the b(10) article; no additional export details\n   - [Export or Transfer Healthie Account Data](https://help.gethealthie.com/article/819-export-your-data) — describes general data export/reporting features, not the b(10) EHI export; notably mentions that \"chat history cannot be exported, except by users of Healthie's API\"\n   - [CCDA Import and Export](https://help.gethealthie.com/article/1214-consolidated-clinical-document-architecture-ccda-import-and-export-on-healthie) — separate ONC certification feature for transitions of care, not the b(10) export\n\n   No additional EHI export documentation was found beyond the single registered page.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nHealthie provides a single, comprehensive documentation page for their (b)(10) EHI export. This is genuine (b)(10) documentation — not a repackaged FHIR API or (g)(10) reference.\n\n### Export Mechanism\n\nThe export produces a **compressed ZIP file** containing CSV files, PDF files, a Documents folder, and an HTML format page, organized per patient. Two export modes are supported:\n\n1. **Single-patient export**: Self-service. User navigates to patient profile > Charting section. Requires the \"Can generate organization report\" permission or non-organization user status.\n2. **Patient population export**: Administrator-only, but **not self-service** — must email hello@gethealthie.com with subject \"Patient Population b10 export request\". Healthie Support handles the export due to \"size of data, time and efforts required to manage server resources.\"\n\nFor population exports, the ZIP contains one directory per patient named `<FirstName><LastName><uniqueidentifier>`, each containing the same files as a single-patient export.\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe export consists of **38 files per patient**:\n- **34 CSV files** with column-level documentation (451 total columns across all files)\n- **2 PDF files**: Charting.pdf (all charting notes) and journal_entries.pdf (all journal entries)\n- **1 HTML file**: format.html (self-referencing export format documentation)\n- **1 folder**: Documents folder (all uploaded documents in original format, preserving folder structure)\n\n### Data Dictionary\n\nThe page contains a complete data dictionary with HTML tables defining every column for each CSV file. For some files, \"Data Notes\" indicate value formats (e.g., \"Year-Mo-Day\", \"true or false\", \"Active or Inactive\") or provide semantic context (e.g., \"Metric categories: Weight, Body Fat %, Waist Circumference, Height (in)\").\n\nNotable structural observations:\n- **Nine journal-type CSV files** (FoodEntry, MetricEntry, MirrorEntry, NoteEntry, PoopEntry, SleepEntry, SymptomEntry, WaterIntakeEntry, WorkoutEntry) all share an identical 21-column schema — a generic entry format with columns like Category, Code, Code System Name, Description, Ed Posthunger, Ed Prehunger, Emotions, etc. The column names suggest this is a single underlying data model for all patient journal entries.\n- **Three food-related allergy CSV files** (Food_Intolerances, Food_Preferences, Food_Sensitivities) share the same 11-column schema as Allergies.csv but with different column naming (Allergen Code System Name vs. System Name).\n- **cms1500s.csv** has 26 columns covering billing claims with insurance policy details, procedure codes, and reimbursement tracking.\n- **Insurance_authorizations.csv** has 23 columns for prior authorization tracking.\n- **All CSV data is exported as strings** — no typed columns.\n\n### Broken Link\n\nThe format.html entry states: \"Within this html page you can find this publicly accessible hyperlink that describes the export format.\" However, the hyperlink points to `#undefined` — a broken anchor. This appears to be a bug in the documentation page; the link was probably intended to point back to the documentation page itself.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nComparing the export files against the product research findings:\n\n**Clearly covered domains:**\n- Demographics and contacts: Client_Overview.csv (13 cols including name, DOB, gender, pronouns, contact info), Addresses.csv, Family_and_Contacts.csv\n- Clinical conditions: Diagnoses.csv (code, active status, onset/end dates)\n- Medications: Medications.csv (name, code, active status, start/end dates, directions, dosage, frequency, route)\n- Allergies: Allergies.csv (allergen code, category, reactions)\n- Care plans: CarePlans.csv (description, name, hidden status)\n- Goals: Goals.csv (description, due date, metric target, repeat, subgoals)\n- Insurance billing: cms1500s.csv (26 cols), superbills.csv (10 cols), Insurance.csv, Insurance_authorizations.csv (23 cols), Policies.csv (19 cols)\n- Payments: Payments.csv (15 cols including amount, currency, refunds, Stripe IDs)\n- Provider information: Provider.csv, Other_Care_Team_Members.csv, Referring_Physicians.csv\n- Messages: Messages.csv (conversation content, timestamps, deletion status)\n- Documents: Documents folder (all uploaded files in original format with folder structure)\n- Charting notes: Charting.pdf (all notes in PDF format)\n- Journal entries: journal_entries.pdf, FoodEntry.csv, NoteEntry.csv, MetricEntry.csv, MirrorEntry.csv, PoopEntry.csv, SleepEntry.csv, SymptomEntry.csv, WaterIntakeEntry.csv, WorkoutEntry.csv\n- Food/nutrition data: Food_Intolerances.csv, Food_Preferences.csv, Food_Sensitivities.csv, FoodEntry.csv\n- Client metrics/biometrics: client_metrics.csv (weight, body fat, waist circumference, height with daily tracking)\n- Client groups: Client_User_Groups.csv\n- Packages: Packages.csv (billing packages with pricing, frequency, visibility)\n- Recommendations: Recommendations.csv\n\n**Domains with potential gaps or ambiguities:**\n\n1. **Lab results**: No dedicated lab results CSV. The product integrates with Rupa Health, Evexia, and Fullscript for lab ordering and results. Lab reports may be captured as documents in the Documents folder, but structured lab data (test names, values, reference ranges) does not appear in the export schema.\n\n2. **E-prescribing data**: Medications.csv captures medication records, but the product's DoseSpot e-prescribing integration likely stores additional prescription-specific data (pharmacy information, prescription status, PDMP queries, refill history) that isn't reflected in the 10-column Medications.csv schema.\n\n3. **Intake forms/questionnaires**: The product has extensive custom intake form capabilities. Intake form data may be embedded in Charting.pdf, but there's no structured CSV export of form responses. For organizations using complex custom forms (e.g., behavioral health assessments, PHQ-9, GAD-7), the PDF format means this data is not machine-readable in the export.\n\n4. **Telehealth session data**: The product supports HIPAA-compliant video sessions. There's no explicit telehealth session file in the export. Session metadata (date, duration, participants) may be captured in charting notes but isn't separately structured.\n\n5. **Immunization records**: The product is certified for (a)(14) implant list which may include immunizations. No dedicated immunizations CSV exists in the export.\n\n6. **Procedures/surgical records**: Procedure codes appear in cms1500s.csv and superbills.csv as billing data, but there's no dedicated clinical procedure record (e.g., procedure notes, outcomes, complications).\n\n7. **Wearable device data**: The product syncs with Google Fit, Apple Health, and Fitbit. The MetricEntry.csv and other journal CSVs have a \"Third Party Source\" column, suggesting wearable data may flow through these files. However, the general \"Export or Transfer\" help article states \"We do not currently support the bulk download of... metrics collected from wearables (outside of what is available in Reports).\"\n\n8. **Supplement recommendations**: The product integrates with Fullscript. Recommendations.csv exists but only has 2 columns (Body, Type) — unclear if this captures supplement-specific data.\n\n9. **AI Scribe transcriptions**: The product offers an AI Scribe feature. Transcription data would likely be embedded in Charting.pdf but is not separately structured.\n\n10. **Appointment/scheduling data**: No appointments CSV in the export. The general export article confirms \"Appointments cannot be exported, however, the Appointments Report can be run to obtain this information.\" While appointment schedules are generally operational data (not EHI), encounter/visit history that documents when care was delivered may be relevant.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Format**: CSV + PDF + raw documents in a ZIP archive. This is a pragmatic, vendor-specific format — not FHIR, not C-CDA, not a standardized schema.\n- **Appropriate for the data?**: Mostly yes. CSV is a reasonable export format for structured tabular data. PDF for charting notes preserves formatting of potentially complex clinical documentation. Raw document export preserves original files.\n- **Key limitation**: No schema file (XSD, JSON Schema, DDL) is provided — only the HTML-based data dictionary on this page. A third party would need to parse the documentation page to understand the CSV column definitions.\n- **Data types**: All CSV values are exported as strings. No type information, no coded value sets, no enumerated values beyond what's in the \"Data Notes\" column.\n- **Relationships**: No foreign keys or explicit relationships between files are documented. For example, cms1500s.csv has a \"Unique ID\" column that presumably links to client records, but this isn't specified.\n- **Reconstructability**: A third party could reconstruct a reasonable picture of the patient record from this export. The CSV structure is flat and readable. However, charting notes are in PDF (not structured) and the lack of explicit relationships between files means some context must be inferred.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n- **Readability**: Good. The page is well-organized with clear sections (EHI definition, export generation, format overview, per-file data dictionary).\n- **Data dictionary**: Complete at the column-name level for all 34 CSV files. Every column is listed. Data notes are provided for some but not all columns (e.g., date formats, boolean indicators, enumerated values).\n- **Missing from documentation**: Data types (all strings), value sets for coded fields, relationships between files, cardinality/nullability constraints, examples for most files (only client_metrics.csv has a screenshot example).\n- **Worked examples**: One embedded screenshot showing client_metrics.csv layout. No sample export files or sample CSV content.\n- **Developer-usable?**: A developer could implement a basic import, but would need to make assumptions about date parsing, coded values, and inter-file relationships. The documentation is sufficient for understanding what data is exported but insufficient for building a robust automated import pipeline.\n- **Maintenance**: The documentation was likely created around December 2023 (based on the nearby release notes mentioning EHI export). The broken `#undefined` link suggests incomplete maintenance.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Column-name level with optional data notes. No data type specifications, no cardinality, no constraints.\n- **Value sets**: Not documented. Fields like \"Current Status\" are noted as \"Active or Inactive\" in data notes, but most coded fields lack value documentation.\n- **Relationships**: Not documented. Files share patient context implicitly (they're in the same patient folder) but inter-file references (e.g., which CMS1500 relates to which charting note) are not specified.\n- **Versioning**: No version number or change history on the documentation.\n\n### Notable Concern: Population Export Not Self-Service\n\nThe b(10) requirement states that the export must be \"self-service and able to be executed at any time the user chooses and without subsequent developer assistance to operate.\" Healthie's population export requires emailing their support team, which appears to conflict with this requirement. Single-patient export is self-service.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nHealthie has made a genuine effort at (b)(10) compliance. This is clearly not a repackaged FHIR API — it's a purpose-built CSV/PDF export that covers the breadth of the platform's data. The data dictionary is thorough at the column level for all 38 export files.\n\nThe export covers the core clinical record well: demographics, diagnoses, medications, allergies, care plans, billing records, messages, and clinical documents. Healthie's distinctive wellness data (food journaling, biometric tracking, sleep/symptom/workout logging) is also included, which is appropriate given these are central to the product's clinical use.\n\nThe main gaps are in structured data for lab results, e-prescribing details, immunizations, and custom intake form responses. The reliance on PDF for charting notes and journal entries means rich clinical data is captured but not machine-readable. The lack of a schema file, explicit relationships, or typed columns limits the export's utility for automated data processing.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://help.gethealthie.com/article/1200-b10-electronic-health-information-export-on-healthie\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (content is in HTML source, not SPA-loaded)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The \"publicly accessible hyperlink\" in the format.html description has a broken `href=\"#undefined\"` — should point to a format specification but doesn't\n- No downloadable artifacts (no PDF, ZIP, JSON schema, or sample files linked from the page)\n- The documentation is entirely contained on a single web page with no supplementary files\n- The general \"Export or Transfer\" article (separate from b(10)) notes several export limitations: chat history only via API, no bulk wearable metric download, no appointment export — some of these may apply to the b(10) export as well\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1366,"cache_read_input_tokens":74161,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1366},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"354678a7-b05b-4118-96a4-c336d8bd88a2","uuid":"eaa23595-d6fb-4929-914a-4f769740d047"}

Policies.csv (19 cols)\n- Payments: Payments.csv (15 cols including amount, currency, refunds, Stripe IDs)\n- Provider information: Provider.csv, Other_Care_Team_Members.csv, Referring_Physicians.csv\n- Messages: Messages.csv (conversation content, timestamps, deletion status)\n- Documents: Documents folder (all uploaded files in original format with folder structure)\n- Charting notes: Charting.pdf (all notes in PDF format)\n- Journal entries: journal_entries.pdf, FoodEntry.csv, NoteEntry.csv, MetricEntry.csv, MirrorEntry.csv, PoopEntry.csv, SleepEntry.csv, SymptomEntry.csv, WaterIntakeEntry.csv, WorkoutEntry.csv\n- Food/nutrition data: Food_Intolerances.csv, Food_Preferences.csv, Food_Sensitivities.csv, FoodEntry.csv\n- Client metrics/biometrics: client_metrics.csv (weight, body fat, waist circumference, height with daily tracking)\n- Client groups: Client_User_Groups.csv\n- Packages: Packages.csv (billing packages with pricing, frequency, visibility)\n- Recommendations: Recommendations.csv\n\n**Domains with potential gaps or ambiguities:**\n\n1. **Lab results**: No dedicated lab results CSV. The product integrates with Rupa Health, Evexia, and Fullscript for lab ordering and results. Lab reports may be captured as documents in the Documents folder, but structured lab data (test names, values, reference ranges) does not appear in the export schema.\n\n2. **E-prescribing data**: Medications.csv captures medication records, but the product's DoseSpot e-prescribing integration likely stores additional prescription-specific data (pharmacy information, prescription status, PDMP queries, refill history) that isn't reflected in the 10-column Medications.csv schema.\n\n3. **Intake forms/questionnaires**: The product has extensive custom intake form capabilities. Intake form data may be embedded in Charting.pdf, but there's no structured CSV export of form responses. For organizations using complex custom forms (e.g., behavioral health assessments, PHQ-9, GAD-7), the PDF format means this data is not machine-readable in the export.\n\n4. **Telehealth session data**: The product supports HIPAA-compliant video sessions. There's no explicit telehealth session file in the export. Session metadata (date, duration, participants) may be captured in charting notes but isn't separately structured.\n\n5. **Immunization records**: The product is certified for (a)(14) implant list which may include immunizations. No dedicated immunizations CSV exists in the export.\n\n6. **Procedures/surgical records**: Procedure codes appear in cms1500s.csv and superbills.csv as billing data, but there's no dedicated clinical procedure record (e.g., procedure notes, outcomes, complications).\n\n7. **Wearable device data**: The product syncs with Google Fit, Apple Health, and Fitbit. The MetricEntry.csv and other journal CSVs have a \"Third Party Source\" column, suggesting wearable data may flow through these files. However, the general \"Export or Transfer\" help article states \"We do not currently support the bulk download of... metrics collected from wearables (outside of what is available in Reports).\"\n\n8. **Supplement recommendations**: The product integrates with Fullscript. Recommendations.csv exists but only has 2 columns (Body, Type) — unclear if this captures supplement-specific data.\n\n9. **AI Scribe transcriptions**: The product offers an AI Scribe feature. Transcription data would likely be embedded in Charting.pdf but is not separately structured.\n\n10. **Appointment/scheduling data**: No appointments CSV in the export. The general export article confirms \"Appointments cannot be exported, however, the Appointments Report can be run to obtain this information.\" While appointment schedules are generally operational data (not EHI), encounter/visit history that documents when care was delivered may be relevant.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Format**: CSV + PDF + raw documents in a ZIP archive. This is a pragmatic, vendor-specific format — not FHIR, not C-CDA, not a standardized schema.\n- **Appropriate for the data?**: Mostly yes. CSV is a reasonable export format for structured tabular data. PDF for charting notes preserves formatting of potentially complex clinical documentation. Raw document export preserves original files.\n- **Key limitation**: No schema file (XSD, JSON Schema, DDL) is provided — only the HTML-based data dictionary on this page. A third party would need to parse the documentation page to understand the CSV column definitions.\n- **Data types**: All CSV values are exported as strings. No type information, no coded value sets, no enumerated values beyond what's in the \"Data Notes\" column.\n- **Relationships**: No foreign keys or explicit relationships between files are documented. For example, cms1500s.csv has a \"Unique ID\" column that presumably links to client records, but this isn't specified.\n- **Reconstructability**: A third party could reconstruct a reasonable picture of the patient record from this export. The CSV structure is flat and readable. However, charting notes are in PDF (not structured) and the lack of explicit relationships between files means some context must be inferred.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n- **Readability**: Good. The page is well-organized with clear sections (EHI definition, export generation, format overview, per-file data dictionary).\n- **Data dictionary**: Complete at the column-name level for all 34 CSV files. Every column is listed. Data notes are provided for some but not all columns (e.g., date formats, boolean indicators, enumerated values).\n- **Missing from documentation**: Data types (all strings), value sets for coded fields, relationships between files, cardinality/nullability constraints, examples for most files (only client_metrics.csv has a screenshot example).\n- **Worked examples**: One embedded screenshot showing client_metrics.csv layout. No sample export files or sample CSV content.\n- **Developer-usable?**: A developer could implement a basic import, but would need to make assumptions about date parsing, coded values, and inter-file relationships. The documentation is sufficient for understanding what data is exported but insufficient for building a robust automated import pipeline.\n- **Maintenance**: The documentation was likely created around December 2023 (based on the nearby release notes mentioning EHI export). The broken `#undefined` link suggests incomplete maintenance.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Column-name level with optional data notes. No data type specifications, no cardinality, no constraints.\n- **Value sets**: Not documented. Fields like \"Current Status\" are noted as \"Active or Inactive\" in data notes, but most coded fields lack value documentation.\n- **Relationships**: Not documented. Files share patient context implicitly (they're in the same patient folder) but inter-file references (e.g., which CMS1500 relates to which charting note) are not specified.\n- **Versioning**: No version number or change history on the documentation.\n\n### Notable Concern: Population Export Not Self-Service\n\nThe b(10) requirement states that the export must be \"self-service and able to be executed at any time the user chooses and without subsequent developer assistance to operate.\" Healthie's population export requires emailing their support team, which appears to conflict with this requirement. Single-patient export is self-service.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nHealthie has made a genuine effort at (b)(10) compliance. This is clearly not a repackaged FHIR API — it's a purpose-built CSV/PDF export that covers the breadth of the platform's data. The data dictionary is thorough at the column level for all 38 export files.\n\nThe export covers the core clinical record well: demographics, diagnoses, medications, allergies, care plans, billing records, messages, and clinical documents. Healthie's distinctive wellness data (food journaling, biometric tracking, sleep/symptom/workout logging) is also included, which is appropriate given these are central to the product's clinical use.\n\nThe main gaps are in structured data for lab results, e-prescribing details, immunizations, and custom intake form responses. The reliance on PDF for charting notes and journal entries means rich clinical data is captured but not machine-readable. The lack of a schema file, explicit relationships, or typed columns limits the export's utility for automated data processing.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://help.gethealthie.com/article/1200-b10-electronic-health-information-export-on-healthie\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (content is in HTML source, not SPA-loaded)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The \"publicly accessible hyperlink\" in the format.html description has a broken `href=\"#undefined\"` — should point to a format specification but doesn't\n- No downloadable artifacts (no PDF, ZIP, JSON schema, or sample files linked from the page)\n- The documentation is entirely contained on a single web page with no supplementary files\n- The general \"Export or Transfer\" article (separate from b(10)) notes several export limitations: chat history only via API, no bulk wearable metric download, no appointment export — some of these may apply to the b(10) export as well\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
